name: Canadian Military Readiness Report — Automated Annual Assessment
author: Canadian Automated Defence Command
description:
CANADIAN ARMED FORCES — ANNUAL READINESS ASSESSMENT
FISCAL YEAR 2199-2200
PREPARED BY: Automated Defence Command, Strategic Assessment Division
CLASSIFICATION: SECRET — NATIONAL DEFENCE

SECTION 1 — PERSONNEL
Active military personnel: 0
Reserve military personnel: 0
Civilian defence employees: 0
Automated defence systems: 2,847 (operational), 412 (standby), 1,203 (decommissioned)
Recruitment status: No active recruitment campaigns. Recruitment infrastructure maintained at standby readiness. Enlistment offices in 47 municipalities remain staffed by automated processing systems. Zero applications received in current fiscal year. Zero applications received in previous fiscal year. Zero applications received in any fiscal year since 2161.

SECTION 2 — EQUIPMENT STATUS
Overall readiness: 88.4% operational
Naval assets: 12 automated patrol vessels (Arctic), 8 automated patrol vessels (Atlantic), 6 automated patrol vessels (Pacific). Hull integrity ranges from 71% to 96%. Weapons systems functional but ammunition stocks at 34% of nominal capacity due to cessation of domestic manufacturing in 2178.
Air assets: 47 automated interceptors (operational), 112 surveillance drones (operational), 23 transport aircraft (standby). Airframe fatigue accumulating at projected rates. Estimated service life remaining: 40-120 years depending on platform.
Land assets: 0 crewed vehicles. 340 automated perimeter defence units. 89 logistics automatons. Equipment degradation rate: 0.4% per annum.

SECTION 3 — THREAT ASSESSMENT
External military threats: None detected.
Internal security threats: None detected.
Border integrity: 99.97% maintained.
Strategic recommendation: Maintain current defensive posture. No escalation required. No de-escalation possible.

SECTION 4 — STRATEGIC PROJECTION
At current equipment degradation rate of 0.4% per annum and zero personnel replacement, Canadian military operational capacity will reach 50% in approximately 110 years and 0% in approximately 235 years. This assessment assumes no external intervention, no equipment replacement, and continued absence of human military personnel. The automated system notes this trajectory and recommends procurement of replacement equipment. The procurement request has been filed annually since 2179. It has not been approved because there is no human authority to approve it. The system will continue to file the request.

[GLMZ NORTHERN DESK NOTE: This document was intercepted from an automated Canadian diplomatic courier delivering the annual defence white paper to treaty allies. The report has been identical in structure for fifteen years. The equipment percentage decreases by exactly 0.4% each year. The system is documenting its own slow obsolescence with perfect bureaucratic precision. It will continue to do so until there is nothing left to document.]
story_hooks: What happens when Canadian military readiness reaches critical thresholds — does the system have contingency protocols?
Could an external force exploit the declining military capacity?
